A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Ouroboros3D, and their main methods and experiments can be matched reliably. However, v1 includes Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix A.1–A.3, whereas v2 refers to supplementary material but ends after the references without including it. This limits comparison of detailed algorithms and formal material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO benchmark results, qualitative reconstructions and feedback ablations in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–8.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional feedback ablations and computational timing measurements in Tables 2–4.

M1.justification: The comparable descriptions retain eight-view SVD generation, time-conditioned LGM reconstruction, RGB/CCM feedback and self-conditioning with probability 0.5. v2 makes supervision views and camera arguments more explicit, but does not establish a changed component, objective or inference procedure.

E1.justification: Objaverse training and GSO evaluation remain unchanged. v2 Figure 8 adds explicit real-world inputs with scene backgrounds, including a horse photograph, extending the qualitative scenarios beyond v1's displayed isolated-object examples.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same accuracy comparators; InstantMesh's shortened table label does not indicate a different method. v2 Table 4 additionally evaluates an SV3D + LGM pipeline for inference speed and standalone SVD/LGM components for computational comparisons.

E3.justification: The main dataset selection, training budget, resolutions, accuracy metrics and 25-step sampling protocol are retained. New experiments restrict feedback to steps 0–25, 10–25 or 20–25 and measure training time per 1,000 steps on an A100 and inference time per sample.

E4.justification: v2 adds an RGB-only feedback control and separate qualitative CCM/RGB comparisons in Table 2 and Figure 7. Table 3 tests when feedback is needed, and Table 4 examines computational overhead. These extend v1's existing joint-training and feedback ablations.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical results are unchanged. Table 2 revises several ablation values, including full-model SSIM from 0.8894 to 0.9094 and LPIPS from 0.1091 to 0.0991, and adds an RGB-only row. Feedback-window and timing results are new. The changed ablation values are not reconciled with v2's unchanged main comparison table.

T1.justification: The main reparameterization and reconstruction-loss equations retain their substance, with more explicit supervision notation in v2. v1's appendix contains diffusion, score-matching and coordinate-map formulations without counterparts in the supplied v2. The missing supplementary material prevents determining whether those formulations were retained, relocated or revised.

C1.justification: v2 adds explicit extensibility to different generation and reconstruction networks to its first contribution. v1 discussed possible reconstruction-module replacement as future work. The central claims about joint recursive diffusion, reduced data bias and improved consistency remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of baseline failure mechanisms, complementary geometry/texture feedback roles and feedback timing. Sections 4.4–4.5 discuss early denoising artifacts and increased training time and memory requirements. The existing mesh-representation and scene-extension caveats are relocated rather than newly introduced.

D1.justification: The supplied documentation loses substantial detail: v1 includes training/sampling pseudocode, EDM noise parameters, coordinate conversion and adapter layer dimensions in its algorithms and appendix. v2 instead refers to an unavailable supplement and also omits v1's explicit VGG perceptual-loss and lambda=1 specifications. It adds eight orbit plus four random supervision views and computational timing details.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive comparisons with Carve3D's reinforcement-learning approach and DMV3D's reconstruction-based denoiser, alongside citations such as Cat3D and MV-Adapter. Several appendix-associated references, including EDM and ControlNet, disappear. The central positioning against separate-stage and inference-only combinations remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental interpretation are extensively rewritten. v2 separates Discussion and Limitation, replaces in-document algorithm descriptions with supplement references, and contains no technical appendix. These changes substantially reshape the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column layout, adds a front-page teaser partly reusing earlier examples, expands the conceptual comparison to three pipelines and redraws the architecture diagram. It restructures the feedback table and figure and adds feedback-window and timing tables. v1's appendix diagrams and architecture table are absent.

improvement.justification: The added feedback controls, timing analysis and cost discussion improve the paper's explanatory evidence. However, the supplied v2 loses substantial reproducibility detail and introduces unexplained disagreement between its full-model ablation values and retained main results. These benefits and deficiencies, together with the unavailable supplement, prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
